quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only under slippery conditions.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use, if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use, if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It is safe to use if you use it the right way.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Ride in the part of the lane that lets other drivers see you as soon as possible.
Always be in the left lane to stay away from oncoming traffic.
Slowly sneak up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is easier to spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the part of the lane that lets other drivers see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in the part of your lane where oncoming drivers will see you first. For example, when approaching a blind corner on your right, ride in the left part of your lane instead of the center.

questions.question: What should you see in your mirrors?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
Your arms.
The road in front of your motorcycle.
The side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane next to you. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: What should you do with a helmet after a crash?

options.text: Inspect it closely.
Replace it.
Sell it to another rider.
Put on a new chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Replace it.
questions.explanation: Always replace any helmet that has been in a crash.

questions.question: How should you hold the handgrips on rough surfaces?

options.text: Hold them loosely to allow for movement.
Hold them firmly to maintain control.
Use lots of throttle to help you get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet as the helmet could become loose and cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold them firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly on rough surfaces to keep your motorcycle under control.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding near stopped or slow cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic begins to move.
Ride on the shoulder to get through quickly.
Weave between the cars to get through quickly.
Do not weave between the cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between the cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between parked or slow cars is dangerous. Car doors might open, or cars might pull into traffic suddenly. You will not have space to move safely. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Do not worry about them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up.
Get off the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can do so safely, change lanes and let a tailgater pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you faster.

questions.question: What does eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not mean they will yield to you when they should.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Many drivers look directly at motorcycles but do not see them.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do?

options.text: Skip using space cushions.
Use more space cushions.
Cut space cushions in half.
Keep enough space cushions around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space cushions around each rider.
questions.explanation: Ride close together as a group, but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually found?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is usually operated with the right foot pedal.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may sound.
The motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
The motorcycle may jerk and a warning light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear too quickly causes the motorcycle to jerk and the rear tire to skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down enough before downshifting.

questions.question: Which item is not protective gear for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Jacket
Boots
Gloves
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Keep your usual space cushion.
Brake later than usual.
Ride slower than usual.
Ride faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger makes your motorcycle sit lower. Ride slower than usual, especially through curves and bumps. The extra weight means it takes longer to speed up, slow down, and stop, so keep a bigger space cushion.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of proper lane positioning?

options.text: It helps you set up for turns.
It gives you an escape route.
It helps you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
It keeps you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots and away from wind blasts. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is usually located near the right footrest.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Make sudden moves.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce speed, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: What happens when a rear tire skids?

options.text: It is not serious.
You lose the ability to steer.
It will fix itself.
It only matters if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to steer.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. When you brake too hard, the rear wheel can lock up. Once it locks, you cannot steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: What does a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It protects your face during a crash.
It only protects you from dirt.
It does not protect as well as goggles.
You should not use it with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your face during a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield also shields you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Often
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear your tire go flat. Instead, you will notice a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can pass in a no passing zone.
You can go 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You must pass on the shoulder if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish passing within the speed limit and only where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: When turning, what happens to your stopping ability?

options.text: You have less grip for stopping.
You have more grip for stopping.
Stopping is the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less grip for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but be very careful. When leaning to turn, some grip is used for turning. This means less grip is available for stopping.
